lines.trans: Here is your station sign, gentlemen: Welcome Back to Room Eight and Room Nine!
Look, Ziad—Nour even drew that exact eight-point compass rose in the corner!
Platform three arrives in twenty minutes, little brother, and the station walk takes twelve.
Will he even remember me from a crowded university lecture hall ten years ago?
Are you kidding, Rami? You recognized his tiny ink star inside one second!
Besides, teachers never forget the quiet student who measures every room in his notebook.
Help carry his suitcase from the platform and take a station taxi straight back here!
Did Mazen manage to invite the neighbours down Jasmine Street for half past three?
Sixteen neighbours already replied yes, and number ten is tuning his violin right now!
Save two seats near the piano for us—come on, Rami, eyes forward and no shortcuts!
Definitely zero Mazen alleys today—straight down Jasmine Street to Central Station!
Ring the gate bell twice when your taxi pulls up at three!

meanings.note: Takes a long -uu-/-oo- stem with possessive endings in Jordanian (أخوي my brother, أخوك your brother); dual أخوين.

examples.trans: My older brother lives in Amman.
The brothers sat together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

أصلا.gloss: anyway; in the first place; actually

meanings.en: anyway; in the first place; actually
meanings.note: Everyday conversational adverb meaning 'in the first place / anyway / to begin with'.

examples.trans: Does the attic even have a comfortable bed?
The wire needed adjusting anyway.

meanings.note: Means 'certainly, definitely' or 'must be' (إنتي أكيد نور 'you must be Nour').

examples.trans: Hello! You must be Nour.

examples.text: أكيد صاحبه رح يدور عليه قريبا.
examples.trans: Surely its owner will look for it soon.

meanings.note: Warm greeting used alone (أهلا!), with فيك/فيكي ('welcome to you!'), or paired as أهلا وسهلا! ('you are most welcome!').

examples.trans: Hello, I am Tariq!
Welcome to Jasmine House!

meanings.note: Warm spoken Levantine affirmation ('yes! / exactly!').

examples.text: أيوا، هاد هو اللحن اللي كنت أدور عليه!
examples.trans: Yes, that's the exact melody I was looking for!

examples.text: أيوا بالزبط، حط الكراسي جنب القوس.
examples.trans: Yes, right there—put the chairs beside the arch.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one man.

examples.trans: Did you plant these herbs yourself?
Did you plan this entire meeting?

meanings.note: Form VIII verbal noun meaning taking a shorter route or shortening a word or process.

examples.text: بلا اختصارات اليوم خلينا نمشي عالجدول.
examples.trans: No shortcuts today—let us stick to the schedule.
In short, the train is going to arrive early.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'twelve'; before a singular counted noun it takes -r: اطنعشر دقة ('twelve chimes').

examples.trans: The clock tower chimed twelve!
Here is twelve dinars change.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Exactly, precisely.

examples.text: هذا اللي كنت بدي أحكيه بالضبط.
examples.trans: This is exactly what I wanted to say.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على بالضبط.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with بالضبط.

meanings.note: Preposition 'without'; followed by ما + verb it means 'without -ing' (بدون ما ياخد 'without taking').

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for a navigation compass (بوصلة النحاس 'the brass compass'). Plural: بوصلات.

examples.trans: The brass compass always stays at the front desk.

examples.text: رسمنا بوصلة صغيرة على بطاقة الترحيب.
examples.trans: We drew a small compass on the welcome card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيانوهات.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تكاسي.

examples.trans: A yellow taxi pulled up at the pavement.
We took a taxi to the bus station.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian possessive word ('belonging to'); agrees in gender: تبع (m.), تبعت (f.), تبعون (pl.).

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتذكر, بيتذكر).

examples.trans: Remember your three simple sentences.
I can remember them easily.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ثواني.

examples.trans: Wait one second, please.
He came back ten seconds later on the dot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from جمع ('to gather'), standard throughout the Arab world for university.

examples.trans: My sister studies engineering at the University of Jordan.

examples.text: الطلاب راجعين من الجامعة الساعة تلاتة.
examples.trans: The students are coming back from university at three.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجراس.

examples.trans: The gate bell rang twice.
Listen to the sound of the bell in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'next to, beside'.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: Used with right and left: الجهة اليمين 'the right side', من هاي الجهة 'from this side'.

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the other side.
Walk this way, it is closer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحبار.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in blue ink.
The ink pen is on the desk.

meanings.note: Before a noun or clause حتى means 'even' (حتى والغرفة فاضية 'even when the room is empty').

examples.text: حتى والغرفة فاضية، السلك بيرن مرتين.
examples.trans: Even when the room is empty, the wire rings twice.
Even room four's bell went quiet!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحجز, بيحجز).

examples.trans: I booked room seven on the phone yesterday.
We booked a quiet dinner at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Form I verbal noun from حمل ('to carry'), meaning the act of carrying or a heavy load.

examples.text: حمل الشناتي التقيلة بده شوية حذر.
examples.trans: Carrying the heavy bags needs a little care.
Help me carry the trays to the table.

meanings.note: Classic Levantine word (from Turkish doğru) meaning 'straight ahead' in directions.

examples.trans: Turn left and walk straight to the bridge.
Walk straight to the end of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Quadriliteral Levantine verb from دوزان ('musical tuning').

examples.text: مدام سعاد بتدوزن أوتار البيانو كل فصل.
examples.trans: Madam Suad tunes the piano strings every season.

examples.text: دوزنا الأوكتاف الوسطاني وصار صوته صافي.
examples.trans: We tuned the middle octave and its tone came out clear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برد, بيرد).

examples.text: اشربي شاي أول وبعدين ردي عالجرس.
examples.trans: Drink tea first and then answer the bell.
Nobody answered the phone at the station.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for drawing a picture, a map or a plan.

examples.trans: He drew me a map to the shop on a piece of paper.

examples.text: بنتي بترسم بيوت وشجر كل يوم.
examples.trans: My daughter draws houses and trees every day.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرصفة.

examples.trans: The car pulled up beside the pavement.
We walked along the wide sidewalk downtown.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرقام.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برن, بيرن).

examples.trans: Someone rang the gate bell!
The old wire always rings twice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: زوايا.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: زحمات.

examples.trans: The breakfast rush finished at ten.
The market has a crowd on Thursdays.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أزقة.

examples.trans: The stone alley is narrow and quiet.
We turned past the narrow lane.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بساعد, بيساعد).

examples.trans: He will surely love to help us!
We helped the guest carry her suitcase.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 16; before a counted singular noun it may appear as سطاش or سطاعشر.

examples.text: مدام سعاد رح تكتب السطاش مازورة الناقصة.
examples.trans: Madam Suad is going to write the sixteen missing bars.

examples.text: صفينا سطاش فنجان أبيض على الرف.
examples.trans: We lined up sixteen white cups on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سنين.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Used both as a masculine adjective ('young traveller' مسافر شاب) and a noun ('young man'). Feminine: شابة, plural: شباب.

examples.text: أسبوع شتا حبس مسافر شاب هون.
examples.trans: A rainy week trapped a young traveller here.
The young people helped carry the chairs to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صغيرة, plural: صغار).

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Arabic numeral 'zero' (source of English 'cipher' and 'zero' via Medieval Latin zephirum).

examples.trans: The temperature dropped to zero at night.
We started counting from zero to ten.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (feminine طالبة, broken plural طلاب), from طلب ('to seek knowledge').

examples.text: الطالب الجديد سأل عن قاعة المحاضرات.
examples.trans: The new student asked about the lecture hall.
The students are reviewing their lessons in the library.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعرف, بيعرف).

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting in two seconds!
Do you know anyone here in Amman?

عزم.gloss: to invite; treat someone to a meal

meanings.en: to invite; treat someone to a meal
meanings.note: Form I verb in everyday Jordanian Arabic for inviting friends over or treating someone.

examples.text: عزمنا الجيران على فنجان قهوة بالعصر.
examples.trans: We invited the neighbours for a cup of coffee in the afternoon.

examples.text: رامي بده يعزم كل الفرقة عالغدا.
examples.trans: Rami wants to invite the whole band to lunch.

meanings.note: Numeral 'ten'; short form عشر ('ashar) before a plural noun (عشر دقايق 'ten minutes').

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Numeral 'twenty' (followed by a singular noun in Arabic: عشرين دقيقة 'twenty minutes').

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Arabic expresses age with عمر + possessive suffix: عمره تمانين سنة ('its/his age is eighty years').

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
He has lived in this quarter all his life.

meanings.note: Verbal noun from عاد ('to return'), used in phrases like حمد لله عالعودة or بعودتك.

examples.text: فرحنا كتير بعودتك بالسلامة يا طارق.
examples.trans: We were very happy at your safe return, Tariq.

examples.text: تذكرة الذهاب والعودة أوفر من المفرد.
examples.trans: A round-trip ticket is cheaper than a single.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; also used in the delighted Jordanian exclamation يا عيني! ('oh my! / how lovely!').

examples.trans: Close your eyes and smell the coffee!
Oh my, look at that warm light in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقيس, بيقيس).

examples.trans: I measure quietness and acoustics in courtyards.
The shopkeeper measured it against the old valve.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قاعات.

examples.trans: The old hall has clear acoustics.
They met in the meeting hall in the morning.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'in front of, before'.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns against the evening sky.
The car is parked in front of the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قريبة, plural: قراب).

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كراسي.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

كمان.gloss: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)

meanings.en: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)
meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'also, too, more' (كمان مرة 'one more time / again').

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Everyday Arabic word for violin (from Persian kamancha), used alongside كمان.

examples.text: زياد بيعزف عالكمانجة من لما كان صغير.
examples.trans: Ziad has played the violin since he was small.
Put the violin in its case after practice.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian conjunction 'when' (in statements, not questions).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لوحات.

examples.text: شوف لوحة المفاتيح الخشب ورا المكتب.
examples.trans: Look at the wooden key board behind the desk.
We wiped the dust off the brass plate.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Form III verbal noun from حضر ('to attend'), used for university classes and public talks.

examples.text: عندي محاضرة تاريخ الساعة عشرة الصبح.
examples.trans: I have a history lecture at ten in the morning.
University lectures started last week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: محطات.

examples.trans: I arrived at the bus station in the morning.
The hotel is close to the station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مرات.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Relative adjective from مركز ('centre'): used in المحطة المركزية ('Central Station') and السوق المركزي.

examples.trans: Let's meet at the Central Station entrance.
The central market is always full of activity.

meanings.note: Masculine verbal noun (masdar) from مزح ('to joke'); used in expressions like بلا مزح ('no kidding').

examples.trans: The jokes are all ordinary teasing.
I'm speaking seriously, not joking.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.text: الشارع على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The street is five minutes away on foot.
Walking in the morning in Amman is enjoyable.

meanings.note: Standalone معقول! is a classic Jordanian exclamation of amazed disbelief ('No way! / Could it really be?!').

examples.text: معقول! قطار جدي الخشب لسا موجود!
examples.trans: Could it be! Grandfather's wooden train is still around!
The price is reasonable and fair for everyone.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نجوم.

examples.trans: The sky is clear and full of stars tonight.
The guesthouse service deserves five stars!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنسى, بينسى).

examples.trans: You forgot the notebook beside the soup bowl.
With all the rush, I completely forgot!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of نصف ('half'); used for half hours (السبعة ونص seven thirty) and quantities (نص كاسة half a glass).

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Lively conversational exclamation of triumph or attention ('ha! / there!').

examples.text: ما صاب قميصي ولا نقطة دهان، ها!
examples.trans: Not a single drop of paint touched my shirt—ha!

examples.text: ها، شو رأيكم باللون الأخضر تحت الشمس؟
examples.trans: Well, what do you think of the green colour in the sunshine?

meanings.note: Masculine هادي ('quiet') is homographic with the feminine demonstrative هادي ('this'); context and agreement distinguish them cleanly.

examples.trans: The spot above the tree is very quiet.
We prepared the quiet attic room for you.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine word for 'here' (لهون 'to here', من هون 'from here').

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Singular form for a flower, highly used in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I picked a rose from the garden.

examples.text: وهذه جملة أخرى طويلة بما يكفي لاجتياز الفحص وتحتوي على وردة.
examples.trans: And this is another long enough sentence to pass the check, with وردة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.text: وقفوا كل شي، قديش الساعة هلا؟
examples.trans: Stop everything — what time is it right now?
The driver pulled the car up by the kerb.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Ubiquitous Jordanian/Levantine encourager ('come on! / let us...!').

examples.trans: Come on, let us bring the bag down into the light!
Let us go check out the room right now!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
